archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pocket-leaning)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose value now comes mainly from intermediate and deep throws and from scrambles, with designed running no longer the engine it was in 2021-2022.

report.headline: Vertical throws still work, the short game broke, and now he's on IR
report.take:
Hurts is a seventh-year dual-threat whose profile has been moving toward the pocket for years. His rushing peaked at 784 yards in 2021 (rank 1) and has fallen steadily to 421 last season. This year he averages 21.4 rushing yards a game, and his designed runs are being stuffed 55.6% of the time at 1.11 yards a carry. The legs still matter on scrambles, which add 0.285 EPA apiece. But the planned run game around him no longer produces.

The passing season splits cleanly in two. Throws of 10+ air yards have been very good: 0.777 EPA per attempt, 6 TDs and +8.7 CPOE, with the intermediate band (0.827 EPA, 62.1% success) as strong as anything in his career. Everything under 10 yards has been bad: -0.266 EPA, -7.1 CPOE, and screens behind the line returning -0.723 a play with 9.1% success. That short game is what normally lets a quarterback live on schedule. So his overall passing EPA sits near zero (rank 29 of 54) even though the downfield work is excellent.

The accuracy collapse is the real story, and it isn't who he has been. He led the league in CPOE in 2024 (+7.5) and was +3.2 last year. Now he is -2.55, with a bad-throw rate of 21.4%, 40th of 42 and 7.1 points worse than last season. The schedule explains part of it. The last three games came against Chicago, the Rams and Jacksonville, defenses ranked 8th, 3rd and 4th by EPA today, and in that stretch his CPOE fell to -9.9 and his EPA per dropback to -0.13, all in losses. He was also pressured on 28.7% of dropbacks (39th of 42) behind an offense ranked 31st in success rate. Some of the dip is opponents and environment. A bad-throw rate that high across easy and hard opponents alike points to something in him, possibly physical, given how the season ended.

That is where it stands. After the Week 5 loss he missed Week 6, started again in Week 7, then gave way to Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III. He is now on injured reserve and listed fourth on the depth chart. The open questions are when he returns and whether the short-area accuracy comes back with him.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep throws carry everything
strengths.body: On 46 attempts of 10+ air yards he has 6 TDs and 0.777 EPA per throw, with completion rates well above expected. The intermediate window has been the best part of his game, with Dontayvion Wicks (0.634 EPA per target) the main beneficiary. His career says he can make these throws. The sample is small, though, and this level of efficiency will cool even when he's healthy.

strengths.title: Scrambles still create value
strengths.body: His legs no longer win on designed runs, but off-script he still turns broken dropbacks into gains: 12 scrambles, 5 first downs, 0.285 EPA each. That helps offset a line allowing heavy pressure. His pressure-to-sack rate (27.1%) sits mid-pack, better than several past seasons.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: Five touchdowns on 14 red-zone attempts, at 0.29 EPA, have kept his TD rate (5.2%, rank 17) above league average despite the poor overall efficiency. It is a thin sample and the most likely number to regress. Still, it reflects his long-standing comfort near the goal line.

concerns.title: Short-area accuracy has fallen apart
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate is 40th of 42, and short throws are losing nearly as much EPA as the downfield throws gain. For a quarterback who led the league in CPOE two years ago, this is a break from his norm rather than a trait. It is the biggest question for whenever he returns, especially if an injury was behind it.

concerns.title: Good defenses exposed him
concerns.body: Against three top-eight defenses he went 0-3 with -0.13 EPA per dropback and -9.9 CPOE. The Rams game (12/27, -18.5 CPOE) was the low point. The schedule explains some of it. But he never found an answer underneath when those defenses took away the deep shots.

concerns.title: Designed run game is gone
concerns.body: Nine designed runs have produced 1.11 yards a carry with more than half stuffed. That fits a multi-year decline in his rushing volume. It removes a dimension that used to shift box counts and leaves him relying on scrambles.

trend.note: He opened with two efficient wins over soft defenses, then slid through three straight losses to top-eight units. Since then he has started only once more and has landed on injured reserve.

nextGame.headline: On IR and fourth on the depth chart: don't expect him
nextGame.body:
Hurts is on injured reserve and listed as QB4 as of November 17, so Pittsburgh at home is almost certainly a game he watches. If he somehow played, the matchup would fit his profile in one way and fight it in another. The Steelers rank 23rd against deep passing, which suits his best throws. They also rank 7th in sack rate against an Eagles line already allowing heavy pressure. Philadelphia is a 4.5-point home underdog with a 38.5 total, a low-scoring script either way.

The supporting cast is thin too. DeVonta Smith (87% of snaps) and Wicks (80%), his two most-targeted receivers, are listed out with a projected return date of the 22nd, game day. Whoever starts may lean on Dallas Goedert against a defense that has struggled with lead tight ends (30th in EPA allowed to TE1). The forecast is early, but it shows gusts near 29 mph and rain showers. If that holds, it would push this further toward the run and keep the passing numbers down.

keyMatchups.title: Sack-heavy front versus porous line
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh's 7.5% sack rate ranks 7th, and the Eagles' quarterbacks have faced pressure all year. Any Philadelphia starter will struggle to hold the ball for the deep shots.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots are the soft spot
keyMatchups.body: The Steelers give up 0.674 EPA on deep throws (23rd), the area where Hurts was at his best. It's a real opening, but probably for a backup.

keyMatchups.title: Goedert against a weak TE coverage
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh allows 0.45 EPA a play to lead tight ends, 30th in the league. With Smith and Wicks listed out, Goedert (0.409 EPA per target from Hurts) is the logical focal point.

nextGame.watch: Any change to Hurts' IR status or practice participation this week; until then, plan around him not playing.

restOfSeason.body:
There is no return date for Hurts in the dossier, only an IR designation and a QB4 depth-chart spot, so the first question is whether he plays again soon. When he does, expect something between this year's version and his career norm. His downfield efficiency will regress from 0.777 EPA on 10+ yard throws, and the red-zone TD rate will cool. His short accuracy, which has been far better every season since 2021, should recover at least partly if the cause was physical. A healthy Hurts probably lands around 170-215 passing yards and 1.0-1.7 touchdowns a game, with rushing stuck in the 15-30 range because designed runs have stopped working.

The environment caps the ceiling. Philadelphia's offense is 29th in EPA, the line allows pressure, and both top receivers are banged up. Fantasy value will lean on TDs and scrambles more than on yardage.
swingFactors: Timing and health of his return from IR
Smith and Wicks getting back on the field

confidence.note: IR with no stated return, five-game sample, sharp break from his career accuracy
